questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I'm currently studying a bachelor's degree in Japan Studies, and so it only made sense to go on exchange in Japan. I felt it was very crucial for my degree to be able to experience living in Japan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy since my host university provided a folder with basically all the information you needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of information, but, unfortunately, a lot of this information was a little difficult to understand at first. It helped a lot to talk with other exchange student's about how they interpreted the information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. My host university helped me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It will be more difficult to establish deep bonds with other exchange students. The exchange students living at Tsukumodai very quickly become friends, and if you live off campus it might take some time to get to know them, since you don't share a way of life.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at the host university was fairly easy. You were given a folder at one of the campuses with all the information needed for registration. There was a lot of information though, which was a little overwhelming.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of help, but the language barrier proved a big problem sometimes. I'm so fortunate that I speak Japanese and it was therefore fairly easy for me to understand, but even then I still sometimes struggled to understand what exactly I was supposed to do, and a lot of times it was difficult for the teacher's or staff to understand what I needed help with. It seemed that there was not a lot of communication between teacher's and staff and others.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all of the courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Registration is quite simple, and there are teacher's to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was very, very low compared to Copenhagen University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at Osaka University was very low quality compared to UCPH, unfortunately. I don't really know why, I'm thinking maybe it was because they had to design a programme for a bunch of exchange student's who came from all over the world, and Osaka University had no idea what level of English student's spoke or what kind of teaching they were used to back home. Personally, I was very bored most of the time. The reading material was more interesting than going to actual classes. I did have one class that was particularly interesting, and I really enjoyed attending that class in person.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Internship course, 2) Literature & Language of Japan and China, 3) Language policies & Multilingual societies in Japan, 4) Japanese Literature, Modern & Contemporary, 5) Approaches to Understanding Culture and 6) Introduction to Japanese Social Sciences.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Japanese Social Sciences. The teacher was just absolutely wonderful and very enthusiastic about the course.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't join any clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I personally didn't join any clubs, but I know that there was a lot of opportunities for all kinds of clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None, since I don't have experience with this.

questions.answer: Travelling.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. But I also study Japan Studies and have been to Japan many times, so I'm very familiar with the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Japanese people are incredibly considerate.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Literally, learn Japanese. Take a Japanese language course, preferably a whole year in advance. And read some books by Japanese authors.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I've gained a much, much deeper understanding of the Japanese way of life, and I'm so thankful that I've been able to experience this. I'm so much more in love with my degree after this exchange semester, and I can't wait to get back to Japan. Actually living in Japan gives you a whole new perspective on Japanese culture, tradition and history. My language skills have gotten much, much better, and I've gained a whole new confidence in my studies.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Completely changing my way of life. I needed to adapt to a whole new way of life and routine, and it was only after 3 months that I felt like I had settled in. One semester was far too little time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I learned that a lot of other European universities won't sent exchange students to Japan unless they agree to do a whole year, simply because they don't believe that 1 semester is enough. I really think UCPH should take this into consideration as well.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
